name: 74HC595 8-bit shift register
description: 8-bit serial-in, parallel-out shift register with a latched (storage) output register and 3-state outputs: clock 8 bits in on SER/SRCLK, pulse RCLK, and QA-QH switch together. Turns 3 GPIOs into 8 outputs (more by chaining through QH'), e.g. for 8 LEDs. Runs on 2-6 V, about 6 mA per output (70 mA total through VCC/GND). Sold as: Texas Instruments SN74HC595N bare chip in a DIP-16 package (pins 1-7 QB-QH, 8 GND, 9 QH', 10 SRCLR, 11 SRCLK, 12 RCLK, 13 OE, 14 SER, 15 QA, 16 VCC), plugged straight into a breadboard.
eli5: Lets your board switch 8 LEDs using only 3 wires: it sends the on/off pattern one bit at a time, then the chip shows all 8 at once.

pins.name: QA

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2-6 V (pin 16). Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico: at 5 V the inputs need 3.5 V for a high

buildNotes: Tie OE (pin 13) to GND and SRCLR (pin 10) to VCC. If either floats, the outputs flicker or stay off (TI: unused inputs must be held at VCC or GND).
Power it from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico. At VCC = 4.5-5 V a logic high must be at least 3.15-3.5 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs are not reliably seen as high.
Each LED needs its own series resistor (330 ohm - 1 kohm). Keep each output under about 6 mA and the whole chip under 70 mA through VCC/GND.
Send 8 bits MSB first on SER, one SRCLK rising edge each, then one RCLK rising edge: bit 7 ends in QH, bit 0 in QA.
Put a 100 nF ceramic capacitor between VCC (pin 16) and GND (pin 8), close to the chip.
Chain chips by wiring QH' (pin 9) to the next chip's SER and sharing SRCLK and RCLK; send the last chip's byte first.

driver.code:
# 74HC595 8-bit serial-in / parallel-out shift register (TI SN74HC595), MicroPython driver.
# Per the datasheet function table: SER is sampled on each SRCLK rising edge (first stage takes SER,
# every other stage takes the previous one), and an RCLK rising edge copies the shift register to the
# output (storage) register. Bits are sent MSB first, so after 8 clocks bit 7 sits in QH and bit 0 in QA.
# Several chips can be chained (QH' of one to SER of the next); the last chip's byte is sent first.
from machine import Pin


class SR595:
    def __init__(self, ser, srclk, rclk, chain=1, srclr=None, oe=None):
        """ser/srclk/rclk/srclr/oe are GPIO numbers. srclr and oe are optional: leave them None when
        SRCLR is tied to VCC and OE is tied to GND on the breadboard."""
        self.ser = Pin(ser, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.srclk = Pin(srclk, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.rclk = Pin(rclk, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.chain = chain
        self.srclr = Pin(srclr, Pin.OUT, value=1) if srclr is not None else None
        self.oe = Pin(oe, Pin.OUT, value=0) if oe is not None else None
        self._state = bytearray(chain)

    def _shift_byte(self, b):
        for i in range(7, -1, -1):
            self.ser.value((b >> i) & 1)
            self.srclk.value(1)  # SER is clocked in on the rising edge
            self.srclk.value(0)

    def latch(self):
        """Copy the shift register to the outputs QA-QH (RCLK rising edge)."""
        self.rclk.value(1)
        self.rclk.value(0)

    def write(self, value):
        """Set all outputs at once. With chain=1 value is 0-255 (bit 0 = QA ... bit 7 = QH);
        with chained chips, bits 8-15 go to the second chip, and so on."""
        for n in range(self.chain - 1, -1, -1):
            b = (value >> (8 * n)) & 0xFF
            self._state[n] = b
            self._shift_byte(b)
        self.latch()

    def value(self):
        v = 0
        for n in range(self.chain):
            v |= self._state[n] << (8 * n)
        return v

    def pin(self, index, on):
        """Switch one output (0 = QA of the first chip) on or off, leaving the others as they are."""
        v = self.value()
        v = v | (1 << index) if on else v & ~(1 << index)
        self.write(v)

    def clear(self):
        """All outputs off. Uses SRCLR (active low) if it is wired, then latches."""
        if self.srclr is not None:
            self.srclr.value(0)
            self.srclr.value(1)
            for n in range(self.chain):
                self._state[n] = 0
            self.latch()
        else:
            self.write(0)

    def enable(self, on=True):
        """Drive OE (active low) if it is wired: outputs on, or high-impedance (all LEDs dark)."""
        if self.oe is not None:
            self.oe.value(0 if on else 1)

from machine import Pin
import time
from sr595 import SR595

sr = SR595(ser={SER}, srclk={SRCLK}, rclk={RCLK})
sr.write(0b00100101)  # QA, QC and QF on
print('OUT=%s' % '{:08b}'.format(sr.value()))
time.sleep(4)
sr.write(0b10000010)  # QB and QH on
print('OUT=%s' % '{:08b}'.format(sr.value()))
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

name: part-74hc595
description: Pinout, electrical limits, wiring and MicroPython driver for the 74HC595 8-bit serial-in / parallel-out shift register (TI SN74HC595N, DIP-16). Use when designing, wiring, simulating or writing code for a 74HC595 in a Sparkbench project or any ESP32 / Raspberry Pi Pico / Raspberry Pi build.
---

# 74HC595 8-bit shift register (SN74HC595N)

## Overview
The **74HC595** turns 3 GPIOs into 8 outputs. You clock 8 bits in on SER/SRCLK into a shift register, then pulse RCLK and the storage register copies them to QA-QH all at once (no flicker while shifting). The outputs are 3-state (OE high = off). Hobbyists buy the bare **Texas Instruments SN74HC595N in a DIP-16 package** and plug it straight into a breadboard, typically to drive 8 LEDs. Chain more chips through QH'.

## Pinout (DIP-16, pin 1 next to the notch)
| Pin | Name | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1-7 | QB-QH | Parallel outputs B to H |
| 8 | GND | Ground |
| 9 | QH' | Serial out, to SER of the next chip when chaining |
| 10 | SRCLR | Shift-register clear, active low: tie to VCC |
| 11 | SRCLK | Shift clock (rising edge) |
| 12 | RCLK | Latch / storage clock (rising edge) |
| 13 | OE | Output enable, active low: tie to GND |
| 14 | SER | Serial data in |
| 15 | QA | Parallel output A |
| 16 | VCC | Supply, 2-6 V |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: 2-6 V (absolute max 7 V); about 80 uA max idle.
- Inputs: high needs >= 0.7 x VCC (3.15 V at 4.5 V), low <= 0.3 x VCC; never above VCC.
- Outputs: specified for 6 mA at 4.5 V (less at 3.3 V); absolute max 35 mA per pin and **70 mA total** through VCC/GND.
- Clock: 5 MHz at 2 V, 25 MHz at 4.5 V (MicroPython bit-banging is far slower, which is fine).

## Interface details
- Function table (datasheet Table 8-1): on each SRCLK rising edge the first stage takes SER and every stage takes the previous one; an RCLK rising edge copies the shift register to the outputs; SRCLR low clears the shift register; OE high puts QA-QH in high impedance.
- Send MSB first: after 8 clocks bit 7 is in QH and bit 0 in QA. Then one RCLK pulse.
- Chained chips: send the far chip's byte first, then the near one, then a single RCLK pulse.

## Wiring
- ESP32: VCC and SRCLR -> 3V3, GND and OE -> GND, SER -> D23, SRCLK -> D18, RCLK -> D5.
- Pico: VCC and SRCLR -> 3V3(OUT), GND and OE -> GND, SER -> GP19, SRCLK -> GP18, RCLK -> GP17.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VCC and SRCLR -> pin 1 (3.3 V), GND and OE -> pin 6, SER -> pin 19, SRCLK -> pin 23, RCLK -> pin 24.
- Each QA-QH output -> 330 ohm-1 kohm resistor -> LED anode, LED cathode -> GND.
- 100 nF ceramic capacitor between pin 16 and pin 8.

## Using the driver
```python
from sr595 import SR595
sr = SR595(ser=23, srclk=18, rclk=5)   # chain=2 for two chips
sr.write(0b00100101)                    # QA, QC, QF on
sr.pin(7, True)                         # QH on as well
```

## Gotchas
- OE and SRCLR must not float: tie OE to GND and SRCLR to VCC (or drive them from GPIOs). Floating inputs give random flicker.
- At 5 V supply a 3.3 V GPIO high is below the 3.5 V threshold: run the chip from 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico.
- Without a resistor per LED the outputs and the 70 mA package limit are overloaded.
- Nothing changes on the LEDs until RCLK is pulsed.
- On some datasheets the pins are named DS, SH_CP, ST_CP, MR, Q0-Q7, Q7' (same pins: SER, SRCLK, RCLK, SRCLR, QA-QH, QH').
